messages:
ana: Heads up — saw a spike in tail latency and egress cost when the allocator hotfilled dedicated slices last night. Proxy sidecars in us-west2 jumped CPU, and egress bytes doubled for ~12m. Not the usual noisy-host signature.
micah: Uh. Any correlating metric IDs? link to grafana? :eyes:
ana: grafana panels: infra.proxy_cpu_pct, infra.egress_bytes/s, allocator.hotfill_events. Spike aligns with hotfill at 03:12 UTC. P95 proxy_latency went from ~20ms -> 180ms for a subset of flows.
devon: Can you paste the proxy logs for that window? quick grep to check handshake/backpressure noise
ops-bot: deploy-bot: new dedicated-pool-hotfill triggered at 2025-03-14T03:12:09Z for pool=dsp-usw2-a
ana: pasted snippets:
```
[03:12:11] proxy us-west2-3 - INFO handshake: backend=dedicated-slice-48 status=connected latency=22ms
[03:12:13] proxy us-west2-7 - WARN handshake: backend=dedicated-slice-49 status=flapping retry=1
[03:12:30] proxy us-west2-3 - ERROR egress: write timeout 300ms
[03:12:40] proxy us-west2-7 - INFO throttle: applied backpressure to tenant=acme-inc drop=0.12%
```
micah: interesting — some proxies flapping while others ok. Could be NIC irq/coalesce or driver spike. What NICs are those hosts on? `kubectl get pods -o wide` might help.
devon: also check kernel dmesg for soft lockups and cpu steal. hotfill may cause sudden cross-tenant burst that hits the sidecar's epoll loop.
ana: ran quick host map, affected nodes share the same top-of-rack switch and one AMD NIC driver version (mlx5 5.15.0-rt). Non-affected are on newer 6.x kernels.
ryan: that rings a bell — last month we saw mlx5 IRQ coalescing regression on 5.15 that amplifies small bursts into large latencies. ops ticket RN-412 documented similar.
micah: ops ticket RN-412 recommended disabling LRO/GRO on kernel < 6.0 for proxies. Can we patch a canary? :thumbsup:
ana: suggested mitigation steps:
- rollback hotfill threshold for DSP pools to avoid mass handoffs (short term)
- canary rolling restart of proxy sidecars on affected nodes with netdev offload toggled
- file a kernel backport ticket with infra-maintainers
devon: quick commands I ran:
```
# check kernel + nic
ssh node-usw2-3 sudo ethtool -k eth0 | egrep 'gro|lro|rx-copy'
# restart sidecar with env tweak
kubectl -n infra set env ds/redwood-proxy NET_OFFLOAD=off --selector=topo=usw2-rack12
```
ana: I rolled the hotfill threshold back at 03:21 UTC and started a rolling restart on 2 nodes as canary. cpu spikes subsided in the restarted nodes, p95 proxy latency dropped back to ~25ms.
ops-bot: alertbot: cost-anomaly: egress-cost-usw2 increased by 2.1x at 03:12 and reduced after 03:26
micah: good quick win. Longer term: we should mesh this into allocator: when hotfill triggers, emit a routing-cost-signal so proxy pool routing stays conservative if NIC kernel version < X. Automated protective routing policy.
ryan: agreed — add a feature flag to allocator to consult host telemetry (kernel, nic driver) and prefer nodes with safe-offload boolean. Also surface a cost-estimate (egress delta) in rollout UI.
devon: note: need to ensure this doesn't overly reduce packing. Let's simulate with the spreadsheet model and a small canary rollout (10% of hotfills) to measure cost/loss tradeoff.
ana: I created a quick task: INFRA-1287 with the mitigation plan and owners (micah for canary, devon for simulator, ryan for allocator change). I'll attach logs and grafana snapshots.
micah: i'm on canary this afternoon. ping me if RN-412 kernel backport lands.
ryan: i'll scope allocator changes, adding telemetry API for node health. rough ETA 1 sprint.
devon: thanks all. TL;DR: proxy jitter caused by NIC+kern combo exposed during hotfill -> short rollback + sidecar restarts mitigated, next steps allocator signal + kernel ticket. :white_check_mark:
ana: thanks — will keep monitor on for 24h and escalate if it reoccurs. :coffee:
